_comment: Storefront paths pa11y-ci audits against the PR's preview theme.
The list is committed rather than crawled so a PR that breaks a page cannot
shrink the audit's own coverage. Selection rule: one path per distinct
TEMPLATE, because a template is the unit a theme change actually alters.
Every product template has exactly one live product, so the handles below are
the whole product surface, not a sample.
The shop-policy pages are the one deliberate exception, with three paths
and template: null. No policy template type exists: Shopify renders all five
/policies/* pages itself inside layout/theme.liquid, which renders
snippets/policy-page.liquid there, and assets/policy-nav.js branches on the
Admin-authored bodies this repo does not control: it builds the jump nav
only at 3 or more h2s. Refund (9 h2s) and privacy (13) take the nav branch;
terms of service and contact information have none and take the hidden one.
So refund covers the nav, terms of service covers the nav-hidden branch on
the largest body in the store, and privacy is here because it is Shopify
auto-managed: its body can change with no commit in this repo. Do not collapse
these back to one path on the strength of the rule above.
When a product handle changes or a template is added, this file must change
with it. scripts/a11y/test/paths.test.mjs asserts every JSON template in
templates/ has an entry here (not just product templates), so a new template
fails the build rather than silently going unaudited, and that every entry's
declared template exists, so a deleted template cannot leave a stale claim
behind. It cannot check handles against the live store (no network in CI unit
tests); a renamed handle surfaces as a 404 in the audit.
Per-entry `ignore` and `hideElements` are pa11y options, passed through by
build-pa11yci.mjs. Use them for third-party embeds this theme does not
control, never to silence a real finding in theme markup.
Top-level `defaults` is the same escape hatch applied to EVERY audited URL.
build-pa11yci.mjs spreads it under the committed pa11y defaults, so it can
add an option but never weaken the standard, the runners, or the Chrome
flags. Reach for a per-entry option first; use this only when the offending
DOM is injected on every page.
Markup this theme cannot reach, hidden from the accessibility tree the
audit walks. Both entries are other people's DOM, which is the ONLY
thing that belongs here: a finding in a file this repo owns gets fixed,
never hidden.
#PBarNextFrame is Shopify's own preview-bar iframe, injected into every
page of a preview theme by the platform. It is title-less and
cross-origin, which is 2 axe findings (frame-title, frame-tested) per
page for markup no template in this repo emits. It does not run on the
live storefront at all.
jdgm- is Judge.me, installed as app blocks (see the
shopify://apps/judge-me-reviews/... types in the product templates). Its
widgets ship an aria-controls pointing at a tab panel that is not in the
DOM until the tab is opened, and a review-form error node whose id is
emitted once per widget on the page. Both are app markup: the theme
renders a block reference, not the HTML, so there is no version of this
repo in which they can be fixed. Matched on class AND id because the
widgets carry the prefix on both and the offending nodes are not all
inside one container.
